question: Which method of contraception can prevent the transmission of HIV?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Barrier methods only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Barrier methods, such as male and female condoms, are effective in preventing the transmission of HIV during sexual intercourse.
 
• Condoms act as a physical barrier, preventing the exchange of bodily fluids that can transmit HIV.
 
• Consistent and correct use of condoms significantly reduces the risk of HIV transmission.
 
• Barrier methods are the only contraceptive method that provides dual protection against both sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and unintended pregnancies.
 
• Other contraceptive methods, like Copper T and oral contraceptives, do not protect against HIV or other STIs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **HIV Transmission**

 
 
• HIV is transmitted through contact with infected blood, semen, vaginal fluids, rectal fluids, and breast milk.
 
• Sexual contact, sharing needles, and mother-to-child transmission are the most common modes of HIV spread.
 
 
 
• **Condom Usage**
 
 
• Using condoms correctly every time during vaginal, anal, or oral sex is crucial for effective protection.
 
• Both male and female condoms are available and provide protection against HIV and other STIs.
 
 
 
• **Other Contraceptive Methods**
 
 
• Copper T (Intrauterine Device) and oral contraceptives are primarily used to prevent pregnancy.
 
• These methods do not offer protection against HIV or other sexually transmitted infections.
 
 
 
• **Dual Protection**
 
 
• Using condoms along with another contraceptive method (e.g., oral contraceptives) provides protection against both unintended pregnancies and STIs.
 
• This practice is known as dual protection and is recommended for sexually active individuals.
